assertion_analysis.fails_if: A dispatched request is refused before three, the fourth is accepted, the refusal changes class or cap, or fewer/more than three pointers are stored; the five fair-share cases rule out the retired share clamp.
The restored session clamp refuses request index 8 (observed in negative-control-final.log), the payload stops reporting a queue position, or the 200 requests are not stored.
The 501st request is accepted, the cap/refusal no longer names queue.max_requests, or awaiting-upstream/blocked-upstream requests are omitted from the held count.
Strict flight validation rejects the queue namespace or resolution drops the override and yields the default; 7 is a literal expectation, not a variable passed through the assertion.
The fallback helper omits the host layer or fails to let the project layer override it; the assertions do not establish that queue_dispatch still calls the helper.
Either MCP read refuses, exceeds its 30-second deadline, or returns fewer/more than the 500 seeded pointers; the returned count independently checks the seeded fixture.

findings.text: The schema addition and companion generated schema, published JSON schema, and legacy test edits are outside prompt.txt:69-75's exclusive write grant; obtain an explicit scope extension or move them into an authorized repair node before landing.

The host/project fallback assertions call _resolved_queue_max_requests directly, so replacing queue_dispatch's use of that helper at reckon/crew/runs.py:753 with the default 500 leaves the added assertions green; fold into an authorized fallback-path test node.
